name: Taurifer UI screen catalog
description: Every user-visible mobile surface, captured from the production UI. Onboarding is covered state by state so no route is represented only by its first screen.

intentionalScrollers.reason: Muscle filters retain a partially visible final chip as a horizontal continuation cue.
Equipment filters retain a partially visible final chip as a horizontal continuation cue.

nonOverlapGroups.reason: The two filter rails and their visible chips may continue off-edge but must not cover one another.

screens.label: One-time landing
screens.scenario: First empty visit. The hero: headline, subtitle, the Build pill, the Track link, three chips and Privacy, with the device-local seen state. The bands below it have their own scrolled states.

screens.label: One-time landing — proof
screens.scenario: Scrolled to the proof: seven steps over the real workout screen with the pinned phone, lens and rail, and the persistent Build control.

screens.label: One-time landing — three ways
screens.scenario: Scrolled to the three ways to start your training: the orange, surface and ink stripes, with the paste hand-off closed.

screens.label: One-time landing — outcomes
screens.scenario: Scrolled to the three engine outcomes (add, hold, back off) with their next targets, and the strength-trend chart.

screens.label: One-time landing — your data
screens.scenario: Scrolled to the ink band: the history stays on the phone, in three rows.

screens.label: One-time landing — questions
screens.scenario: Scrolled to the questions with the RIR answer open.

screens.label: One-time landing — close
screens.scenario: Scrolled to the closing orange band with the Build pill and the Track link; the persistent Build control has stepped aside.

screens.label: Returning landing
screens.scenario: A later visit to a device with no program and no log, with nothing saved. The welcome-back headline and its line, the Build pill, the Track link and Privacy lead; the chips, the proof and the outcomes are left out, and the ways, the data promise, the questions and the closing band follow.

screens.label: Returning landing — setup saved
screens.scenario: A later visit with a half-finished Recommend setup saved. The lead action names it (Continue choosing your program) in the hero and the closing band; tapping it opens the chooser's resume card.

screens.label: Entry hub
screens.scenario: Create a program. Recommend is the sole primary path; Custom is its generated alternative; Browse stands alone; Bring or build is collapsed.

screens.label: Entry hub — own disclosure open
screens.scenario: The Bring or build disclosure expanded with aria-expanded to reveal Build, paste, and Taurifer-file import paths.

screens.label: Entry hub — existing program
screens.scenario: Opened from Settings while a program is active, so replacement consequences are in view.

screens.label: Entry hub — route help open
screens.scenario: The Not sure which one? helper expanded on the hub: two short questions that end in Continue with the suggested route, reaching all five jobs.

screens.label: Recommend 1 — desired result
screens.scenario: Route header, Cancel, progress 1 of 5, three desired-result choices.

screens.label: Recommend 2 — training background
screens.scenario: The carried goal with Change, then structured-program experience and recent six-week consistency.

screens.label: Recommend 3 — real week
screens.scenario: Days per week, session-minute ceiling, preferred rest.

screens.label: Recommend 4 — environment
screens.scenario: Environment shortcuts with the capability correction disclosure closed.

screens.label: Recommend 4 — equipment correction
screens.scenario: The capability correction disclosure open.

screens.label: Recommend 5 — priorities
screens.scenario: Primary priorities plus optional movement and exercise-avoidance controls.

screens.label: Recommend 5 — avoidance and pain safety
screens.scenario: One avoided exercise with the pain reason selected and its safety copy.

screens.label: Recommend — recommendation and review
screens.scenario: The program first: name, four facts, the week with its first day open, the answers it was built from as chips, why it fits, and the pinned activation.

screens.label: Recommend — recommendation with a program active
screens.scenario: The merged candidate surface while the current program remains untouched.

screens.label: Recommend — answer editor open
screens.scenario: The review with the days-per-week chip open on its inline editor: the same numeric cards as the question, an Update program action, and the pinned activation set aside.

screens.label: Recommend — after a changed answer
screens.scenario: A changed answer rebuilt the program in place: the change statement with Before and Now, an added exercise tagged new, and its day open.

screens.label: Recommend — after avoiding an exercise
screens.scenario: An exercise the program contained is avoided from the priorities editor: the statement, and the constraint line with Restore.

screens.label: Recommend — confirm replacement
screens.scenario: The explicit archive-and-replace confirmation. History is not changed.

screens.label: Recommend — activation conflict
screens.scenario: Another tab changed the active program. The newer program stays active.

screens.label: Custom 1 — desired result
screens.scenario: The custom route's own header and step count, not Recommend's.

screens.label: Custom 2 — training background
screens.scenario: Structured-program experience and recent consistency in the custom route.

screens.label: Custom 3 — real week
screens.scenario: Days per week, session ceiling and preferred rest in the custom route.

screens.label: Custom 4 — environment
screens.scenario: Environment shortcuts in the custom route.

screens.label: Custom 5 — muscle priorities
screens.scenario: Each muscle has one accessible emphasis setting before exercise preferences.

screens.label: Custom 6 — exercise preferences
screens.scenario: One library search offers Include or Avoid, with separate selected lists.

screens.label: Custom 6b — weekly structure
screens.scenario: Two compatible weekly structures to choose from; shown only when more than one fits the answers.

screens.label: Custom — generated program and review
screens.scenario: The custom program first, with muscle emphasis and exercise preferences among the answer chips, and the pinned activation.

screens.label: Browse 1 — real week
screens.scenario: Days per week and session length, the only questions Browse asks.

screens.label: Browse 2 — environment
screens.scenario: Environment shortcuts before the catalogue is filtered.

screens.label: Browse — catalogue
screens.scenario: Released, complete, tested programs with purpose, frequency and mismatches.

screens.label: Browse — review
screens.scenario: The common review surface for a catalogue program.

screens.label: Build 1 — name and days
screens.scenario: The build_setup step: program name and day count before the editor opens.

screens.label: Build — empty days
screens.scenario: Real empty day containers, Add exercise, Save draft, activation disabled.

screens.label: Build — partial draft
screens.scenario: One populated day and one incomplete day. Activation stays disabled.

screens.label: Build — activation ready
screens.scenario: A complete manual draft with supported progression and activation enabled.

screens.label: Import — source
screens.scenario: The bounded supported-file and setup-source surface before any mutation.

screens.label: Import — paste a program
screens.scenario: The free-form door as it opens: an empty field, and the hand-off to ChatGPT or Claude still unavailable.

screens.label: Import — paste ready to convert
screens.scenario: A pasted program with both app links live, the character counter, and the field the reply comes back into.

screens.label: Import — choose an assistant
screens.scenario: Stage 2 with collapsed source summary, Edit button, ChatGPT and Claude buttons, and Preview prompt disclosure.

screens.label: Import — paste reply
screens.scenario: Stage 3 with collapsed source summary, Import from clipboard, the "or paste" divider, reply textarea, Review CTA, Try another assistant, and Start over.

screens.label: Import — resolve gaps
screens.scenario: Gap resolution screen with inputs for missing sets and reps, and the non-imported disclosure.

screens.label: Import — gap validation error
screens.scenario: Gap resolution screen after submitting empty inputs, highlighting invalid fields with .is-invalid and aria-invalid.

screens.label: Import — unreadable reply
screens.scenario: Unreadable reply recovery block with Copy repair prompt and Try another assistant actions.

screens.label: Import — exercise review
screens.scenario: Reviewing candidate matches: collapsed candidate chips, disclosure expanded, and unmatched flat escape hatches.

screens.label: Import — review
screens.scenario: A mapped exercise with manual progression ownership and provenance.

screens.label: Shared setup — adaptive landing
screens.scenario: An incoming setup link adapts the landing around its safe program summary. Nothing persists until Start.

screens.label: Shared setup — invalid landing
screens.scenario: An invalid setup link explains that nothing was saved and keeps safe Build and Track actions available.

screens.label: Shared setup — review
screens.scenario: The editable preview a shared payload lands in before explicit activation.

screens.label: Resume setup
screens.scenario: The resumable notice after reload: route, step, recency, Resume, Start over.

screens.label: Rules changed
screens.scenario: A draft whose compiler rules are stale. Rebuild is required before activation.

screens.label: Cancel setup — keep or discard
screens.scenario: Cancel pressed mid-flow. A dialog over the current step asks whether to keep the draft or discard it; Escape or Continue setup returns to the step.

screens.label: Start over — confirm
screens.scenario: Start over pressed on a review. A dialog asks before the answers and the unused program are discarded; the active program does not change.

screens.label: Today — no program
screens.scenario: A fresh device after leaving setup, with no program or workout controls.

screens.label: Today — ready to start
screens.scenario: The Direction D lifter before Day 1 starts: the prescription table reads recommendation() for every exercise, with the verdict tally above it.

screens.label: Today — mixed strategies
screens.scenario: The Direction D mixed day: anchor and back-off, rep goal, fixed effort, a manual slot in soft ink with no mark, a custom exercise and a lift with a set logged without RIR.

screens.label: Today — running rest bar
screens.scenario: The rest countdown remains visible after leaving the active workout.

screens.label: Today — choose another day
screens.scenario: The day picker sheet open.

screens.label: Today — session complete
screens.scenario: The state after the day's session is logged.

screens.label: Workout — focus mode
screens.scenario: One exercise at a time.

screens.label: Workout — Focus glossary definition
screens.scenario: A definition is open after tapping a glossary term in Focus.

screens.label: Workout — stale draft recovery
screens.scenario: A conflicting tab won while this tab retains a pending field value and offers Reload latest or Copy value.

screens.label: Workout — draft persistence retry
screens.scenario: A field write was interrupted; the exact pending value remains visible beside Retry and Copy value actions.

screens.label: Workout — invalid draft recovery
screens.scenario: An unreadable local draft remains untouched and offers a non-destructive copy action.

screens.label: Workout — rest running
screens.scenario: A logged set has started the rest: the clock, the drain bar and the next set's cue take the cue slot, and the rest controls take the shelf's pad row.

screens.label: Workout — rest done
screens.scenario: The rest has run out: the clock collapses to one line that counts the overrun up, the cue returns and the field pads come back.

screens.label: Workout — exercise note
screens.scenario: The per-exercise note sheet.

screens.label: Workout — why this weight
screens.scenario: The recommendation inspector for a range lift: sentences first, each under a bold lead, the working behind See the working, the evidence footer.

screens.label: Workout — why this weight, mid-session
screens.scenario: Opened after set 1 is logged: what the set showed (the observed capacity) before the prediction for the next set.

screens.label: Workout — why this weight, rep goal
screens.scenario: Rep goal: the total, the effort gate and how the reps split.

screens.label: Workout — why this weight, anchor and back-off
screens.scenario: Anchor and back-off: the performed top set, the rule, and the percentage that sets the lighter sets.

screens.label: Workout — why this weight, manual
screens.scenario: Manual: one sentence; the program sets the load and the engine does not change it.

screens.label: Session summary
screens.scenario: The Direction D lifter's Day 1 summary: an outcome word per lift, the sets, records in green and the next target as the strongest line.

screens.label: Session summary — maintained
screens.scenario: A finished Day 2 whose Romanian deadlift is maintained, with its other lifts improved and a record.

screens.label: Session summary — declined
screens.scenario: A finished Day 3 that reports declined lifts in ink, without turning the result into a prescription.

screens.label: Session summary — mixed strategies
screens.scenario: The Direction D mixed day finished: anchor and back-off, rep goal, fixed effort, a manual lift and a custom exercise, with improved and maintained words, a lift without RIR and its records.

screens.label: Session summary — first session
screens.scenario: Every lift is a first exposure: the baseline sentence, no outcome words, and the next targets from the engine.

screens.label: Progress — overview
screens.scenario: The Progress landing tab.

screens.label: Progress — baseline-building overview
screens.scenario: Sparse evidence remains neutral and contributes no Needs action items.

screens.label: Progress — actionable overview
screens.scenario: Sufficient evidence produces linked program-wide action items.

screens.label: Progress — exercise chart
screens.scenario: A single lift's strength chart.

screens.label: Progress — Strength
screens.scenario: The Strength sub-tab.

screens.label: Progress — Strength current block
screens.scenario: Current-block values, outcomes, and drill-in share one scope.

screens.label: Progress — Strength all history
screens.scenario: All-history scope explicitly includes archived observations.

screens.label: Progress — Strength comparison
screens.scenario: Two compatible points show values, dates, absolute change, and percentage change.

screens.label: Progress — Strength sparse evidence
screens.scenario: Zero or one compatible point remains neutral baseline evidence.

screens.label: Progress — Volume
screens.scenario: The Volume sub-tab and its muscle rows.

screens.label: Progress — Volume block to date
screens.scenario: Block-to-date volume uses elapsed weekly prescriptions.

screens.label: Progress — Volume muscle detail
screens.scenario: A primary muscle row expands to its scoped session evidence.

screens.label: Progress — PRs
screens.scenario: The personal-record list.

screens.label: Progress — PR detail
screens.scenario: A personal record expands to locale-formatted evidence detail.

screens.label: Progress — Review
screens.scenario: The mesocycle review surface.

screens.label: Progress — active Review
screens.scenario: The active-block checkpoint is read-only.

screens.label: Progress — completed-block Review
screens.scenario: A completed block exposes the evidence-valid structural routes.

screens.label: Progress — insufficient-evidence Review
screens.scenario: A completed block with sparse evidence excludes performance-derived actions.

screens.label: Progress — schedule diagnosis
screens.scenario: The one-question choice between fewer days and shorter sessions.

screens.label: Progress — lower-frequency preview
screens.scenario: A provenance-backed lower-frequency sibling diff before confirmation.

screens.label: Progress — shorter-session preview
screens.scenario: A provenance-backed shorter-session sibling diff before confirmation.

screens.label: Progress — guided repair staged
screens.scenario: The exact current program is staged for explicit guided editing.

screens.label: Progress — volume-reduction preview
screens.scenario: The protected permanent-volume reduction diff before confirmation.

screens.label: Progress — recovery eligibility
screens.scenario: Recovery stays unavailable without sufficient qualifying pattern evidence.

screens.label: Progress — recovery readiness question
screens.scenario: Eligible pattern evidence still requires the explicit local readiness answer.

screens.label: Progress — recovery preview
screens.scenario: The policy-versioned week-one prescription diff before confirmation.

screens.label: Progress — active recovery week
screens.scenario: The confirmed recovery overlay is visible during week one.

screens.label: Progress — recovery reassessment
screens.scenario: Canonical week two asks Better, About the same, or Worse.

screens.label: History
screens.scenario: The logged session list.

screens.label: History — expanded session
screens.scenario: One session expanded in place.

screens.label: History — dirty edit
screens.scenario: A session edit with an unsaved canonical change and its destructive actions still visible.

screens.label: History — invalid edit
screens.scenario: An invalid set value is held at the field boundary with the editor's validation state visible.

screens.label: History — confirmed delete
screens.scenario: The explicit delete confirmation surface for one selected session.

screens.label: History — edit conflict
screens.scenario: A stale session edit refuses to overwrite a newer durable change and offers recovery actions.

screens.label: Exercise library
screens.scenario: The searchable movement library.

screens.label: Exercise library — selected movement
screens.scenario: One movement is selected and the persistent add bar is visible.

screens.label: Exercise library — preview
screens.scenario: An illustrated movement preview.

screens.label: Exercise library — detail
screens.scenario: The full movement detail surface.

screens.label: Exercise library — detail glossary definition
screens.scenario: A definition is open after tapping a term in movement detail.

screens.label: Program — no program
screens.scenario: A fresh device's Program tab, with setup as the only action.

screens.label: Program
screens.scenario: The current program and its days.

screens.label: Program — editor
screens.scenario: The installed program editor, with the first day open.

screens.label: Program — exercise picker
screens.scenario: The picker sheet.

screens.label: Program — custom exercise
screens.scenario: The custom movement sheet.

screens.label: Program — saving a custom exercise
screens.scenario: A new custom movement is saving; its actions stay unavailable until the durable write settles.

screens.label: Program — deleting a custom exercise
screens.scenario: A custom movement is deleting; the action names deletion and all competing actions stay unavailable until the durable write settles.

screens.label: Program — archiving a custom exercise
screens.scenario: A custom movement referenced by a performedMovementId-only history row is archiving; the action names archive and preserves its history identity.

screens.label: Program — recovering a custom exercise change
screens.scenario: A partial archive stays visibly unresolved with recovery status, Retry recovery, and Reload actions.

screens.label: Program — share setup link
screens.scenario: The setup-link share sheet.

screens.label: Program — share with one blocker
screens.scenario: The share sheet names one unresolved exercise and keeps copy/share unavailable.

screens.label: Program — repair returns to Share
screens.scenario: The custom repair path has been cancelled and returns directly to the blocked Share sheet.

screens.label: Program — share link ready
screens.scenario: A valid setup link is ready for copy or system sharing.

screens.label: Program — text export
screens.scenario: The plain-text program export sheet.

screens.label: Settings
screens.scenario: The settings list.

screens.label: Settings — Appearance
screens.scenario: The appearance/theme row.

screens.label: Settings — contextual guides
screens.scenario: The per-guide replay controls; replay changes presentation state only.

screens.label: Settings — replayed guide
screens.scenario: A real contextual guide replayed from Settings and anchored to its live privacy action.

screens.label: Settings — privacy and analytics
screens.scenario: The privacy and analytics section.

screens.scenario: The cached ADR 0013 disclosure reached from Settings.

screens.scenario: The pre-action transfer explanation and explicit consent.

screens.scenario: Transfer creation in progress.

screens.scenario: Successful creation followed by Safari installation instructions.

screens.scenario: A definitive pre-create failure with retry and install-without-transfer actions.

screens.scenario: The installed app is claiming its one-time transfer.

screens.scenario: The installed app is atomically importing the clone.

screens.scenario: Verified local import and remote deletion are complete.

screens.scenario: Local import succeeded while verified remote deletion still needs retry.
